gap_text: mcporter recovery required intervention after stale metadata refusal and a startup timeout; automatic recovery was not established.
next_check: On an owned disposable mcporter daemon (0.13.13 and 0.14.0), induce stale metadata and a startup timeout, and record whether the next call recovers without manual intervention.

preregistration.expectation: On owned daemons for both 0.13.13 and 0.14.0: after SIGKILL (stale metadata) the next call is refused with no replacement launched; after a SIGSTOPped (unresponsive) daemon the next call times out; neither recovers without manual intervention (archiving metadata / killing the stopped process). Daemon client code is byte-identical, so both versions behave the same.
preregistration.criteria: settled if both inductions were run on both versions and the next-call behavior plus the minimal manual step were recorded; the answer to 'automatic recovery' is whatever is observed.

addenda.label: added arm, written after the first lifecycle runs (04:09-04:14Z) and before this arm ran
addenda.expectation: With the daemon stopped and daemon/user.json.lock held by a live owned process (sleep), a call launches a daemon whose host blocks in withFileLock (dist/fs-json.js, DEFAULT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS 30000) so the client readiness wait fails; after the holder exits the lock is recoverable (dead pid) and the next call starts a daemon with no manual step, unless the failed start left metadata behind, in which case the stale-metadata refusal applies.
addenda.criteria: Record the first call's exit/elapsed/stderr and whether the next call after the holder exits succeeds without any manual step. Run on 0.13.13 and 0.14.0.

addenda.label: FIX ROUND 1, written after the round-1 independent review (raw/review-codex-round1.txt, received 04:35:13Z) and before the fix-round runs
addenda.expectation: Re-running the bridge matrix, both lifecycle fixtures and the unmodified-config arm inside unshare -rnm with an empty tmpfs mounted over $HOME/.mcporter (the shared daemon's socket path does not exist there) gives the same outcomes. A connect probe to the shared socket path inside the namespace returns ENOENT, while the same probe against the owned daemon socket connects. That owned control shows the probe detects a reachable socket. wong2 interactive listing is executed x3 for all 5 servers and renders at most one page (10 tools). With a lock holder that EXITS ON ITS OWN (sleep with a fixed lifetime, no harness kill), a call made while the lock is held times out after 45 s, a second call while still held also fails, and the first call after the holder exits succeeds with no step taken by the harness or the operator.
addenda.criteria: Gap 10 and the no-contact claim in the other receipts are settled only by the enforced (tmpfs + netns) runs with the probe and owned control recorded. Gap 12/6: settled only if every wong2 list arm executed (interactive), with incompleteness reported as a result. Gap 9: the startup-timeout conclusion is restated to match what the natural-expiry arm shows.

note: Both inductions ran on owned daemons for 0.13.13 and 0.14.0, with identical results. Stale metadata after SIGKILL is refused on every following call, and one manual step (archiving daemon/user.json) is required: no automatic recovery. Startup timeout: while daemon/user.json.lock is held by a live process, two consecutive calls each fail after about 45 s ('did not become ready within 45 seconds'). The holder has a fixed lifetime and exits on its own (fix round 1: the harness does not kill it). The first call after that succeeds with no harness or operator step. So mcporter recovers automatically once a startup obstruction clears, but never from stale metadata. The SIGSTOP arm is disclosed separately: calls time out after 60 s, and the harness then kills the stopped daemon, which leaves the stale-metadata case.
limits: Servers ran with owned state only (temp HOME/XDG, MCPORTER_DAEMON_DIR under $HOME/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923, owned ai-memory --data-dir and Qdrant storage). Fix round 1 runs are ENFORCED: unshare -rnm with an empty tmpfs over $HOME/.mcporter and a fresh network namespace (enforce.py / ns_exact.py). Inside, an AF_UNIX connect to the shared daemon socket path returned 'FileNotFoundError: No such file or directory' and TCP 49374/16333 returned 'ConnectionRefusedError: Connection refused', while the same AF_UNIX probe against each owned daemon socket returned ['connected'] (owned control, so the probe can detect a reachable socket). Round-1 runs (raw/round1/) set only environment-level isolation; their stat() of the shared daemon (pid, socket inode, metadata mtime) could not detect a client connection, so they are not cited for the no-contact claim.
/tmp was not isolated; SocratiCode reported another process watching the agent-lab checkout, i.e. it read host watcher state.
The startup-timeout arm was added by addendum at 04:14:45Z and changed in fix round 1 (04:36:13Z) so that the lock holder exits by itself; round-1 files are in raw/round1/.
Inductions are SIGKILL, SIGSTOP and a held lock; the WSL-reboot incident of 2026-09-19 was not reproduced.
